panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Clinical photograph of the patient’s dorsal hands showing keratotic lesions at the metacarpophalangeal joints and wrist; the article concerns Vohwinkel syndrome and the caption describes these as part of the clinical presentation. B: Clinical photograph of bilateral palmar keratoderma with honeycomb appearance, a characteristic cutaneous manifestation of Vohwinkel syndrome. C: Clinical photograph of pseudoainhum involving the toes, a recognized mutilating feature of Vohwinkel syndrome. D: Clinical photograph of bilateral starfish-shaped keratotic lesions on the dorsal feet, a classic manifestation of Vohwinkel syndrome. E: Hematoxylin and eosin histopathology from the patient’s elbow plaque showing orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis; this is a tissue-level correlate in a case of genetically confirmed Vohwinkel syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Duran-Lemarie et al. Vohwinkel syndrome with de novo heterozygous mutation in the GJB2 gene - c.175G>A (p. Gly59Ser).. Anais brasileiros de dermatologia 2025. doi:10.1016/j.abd.2023.01.010. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Physical examination and histopathology image. (A) Bilateral linear keratotic lesions at dorsum of metacarpophalangeal joints and right wrist. (B) Bilateral palmar keratoderma with “honeycomb” appearance. (C) Pseudoainhum at third and fourth toes. (D) Bilateral dorsal feet starfish-shaped keratotic lesions. (E) Orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis. (Hematoxylin & eosin, ×100).
in_text_mentions: examination revealed palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with a honeycomb appearance, and bilateral linear and starfish-shaped keratotic lesions on the dorsum of his feet and the metacarpophalangeal joints (Fig. 1). Keratotic plaques on elbows and knees were also seen. There was no family history of similar skin lesions or hearing loss. A genomic DNA sample was obtained from peripheral blood leukocytes. Histopathological analysis from his elbow plaque revealed orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis (Fig. 1).
